title: Christie's historical scientific and natural-history lot archive audit
purpose: Record a bounded lot-level web-index audit of the high-priority Christie’s South Kensington scientific/model/natural-history catalogue family before full catalogue scans are obtained.
coverage_guard: This file records search-engine and currently indexed Christie’s lot-page coverage only. It is not a complete catalogue screen. A sale may be called lot-text negative only after its full catalogue or complete lot browse has been inspected.

indexed_archive_findings.statement: A surviving Christie’s lot page for a Philippe Danfrie astrolabe cites the 8 April 1998 South Kensington catalogue 'Exceptional Scientific and Engineering Works of Art, Instruments and Models' and lot 50.

A surviving Christie’s model-locomotive lot page carries an end-of-sale notice for the 7 April 2005 'Exceptional Scientific and Engineering Works of Art, including Natural History and the William L. Camp Jr Spectacle Collection' sale; independent academic literature cites a scientific instrument sold there as lot 586.
indexed_archive_findings.lot_number_evidence_note: Lot 586 comes from later scholarly provenance for a Coignet nocturnal, not from a complete sale browse.

indexed_archive_findings.statement: A surviving Christie’s pocket-globe lot page cites 'Scientific, Medical and Engineering Works of Art and Natural History', sale catalogue 5650, 19 October 2005, lot 140.

Searches for model/glass/natural-history terms inside the historical scientific-sale family recover locomotives, globes, microscopes, bottles, instruments and other models. This confirms that object-class search has broad recall but requires lot-level maker/material review.

blaschka_result.result_wording: No additional qualifying pre-2019 physical Blaschka glass-model lot was recovered from the currently indexed Christie’s historical lot pages in this pass.
blaschka_result.important_guard: This is a bounded public-index result. It does not close any of the target catalogues because search-engine indexing may omit lots and Christie’s browse-lot pages are not fully exposed in the text runtime.

next_actions: Obtain issue-level access to the 1997-2001 and 2002-2006 Christie’s scientific/model runs held by Museo Galileo before buying commercial scans.
If remote catalogue images are available, OCR and screen the whole 1997, 1998, 1999, April 2005, June 2005 and October 2005 catalogues with the full query vocabulary.
Where Christie’s sale landing pages expose a numeric Browse lots count, do not treat that count as the printed catalogue lot count unless the sale identity/date is independently matched.

Retain unrelated anatomical/scientific models as category controls only when they illuminate search contamination; do not add them to the Blaschka false-positive corpus unless the maker name appears or attribution is Blaschka-adjacent.
